intended_object: For a profinite group G and a G-representation A over R, the inverse limit lim_U H_n(G/U, A^U) over open normal subgroups U, taken along the deflation maps (coinflation followed by the norm A^U → A^V), as a topological R-module. For n ≥ 1 this is the usual definition of negative-degree Tate cohomology Ĥ^{-n-1}(G, A) of a profinite group (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg). This reading comes from the docstring, the module docs and docs/FiniteTateDiagrams.md.
explanation:
The definition is `limit (topologicalFiniteNegativeDeflationDiagram A n)`, a limit in `TopModuleCat R`. The diagram is indexed by `OpenNormalSubgroup G`. At S its value is `groupHomology (A.quotientToInvariants S) n`, i.e. H_n(G/S, A^S), with the module topology on it.

For S ≤ T, the transition map is `finiteNegativeDeflation`. It is coinflation H_n(G/S, A^S) → H_n((G/S)/(T/S), (A^S)_{T/S}), then the map induced by the norm (A^S)_{T/S} → (A^S)^{T/S}, then the identifications (G/S)/(T/S) ≅ G/T and (A^S)^{T/S} ≅ A^T. This is exactly the standard deflation map on homology. Its covariant direction, from smaller to larger subgroups, is the right one for an inverse limit.

So the object is lim_U H_n(G/U, A^U) along deflations. This is the standard definition of homology and negative-degree Tate cohomology for profinite groups, and the docstring says only that it "models" Tate degree -n-1 for positive n.

Generality is natural:
- Profiniteness is used, because open normal subgroups have finite index and the norm needs a finite T/S.
- The ring R is an arbitrary topological commutative ring.
- The module topology on each stage is the canonical choice; it is discrete when R is discrete, as in the classical setting.

Mathlib has no profinite group homology or profinite Tate cohomology to compare against. The definition is a thin, correct wrapper around a categorical limit.
